__broaden__.εἶεν: εἰμί — be; pres. opt. 3 pl., in an indirect question: ’(who) they might be’ · also with κε, potential: ’would be’ (κ’ … εἶεν) · also in a concessive condition after εἰ: ’were’ (οὐδ’ εἴ οἱ χεῖρες … εἶεν ’not even if he had hands’) · also in a wish with a dat. of the person: ’may (they) be’ (ἔνδον ἑταῖροι εἶεν ’may my companions be inside’)
__broaden__.θέρος: θέρος — summer; neut. nom. sg. · also neut. acc. sg., after ἐς: ’by summer’ (ἐς θέρος)
__broaden__.κέν: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν); accented before an enclitic · also + aor. indic., unreal past: κέν μοι … κατέχευας ’you would have poured on me’ · also + subj. in a main clause: ’may’ (καί κέν οἱ ὑπέρσχῃ χεῖρα ’and he may hold his hand over him’) · also + opt., potential: ’would’ (κέν μοι … εἴη ’would be mine’)
__broaden__.κακὸν: κακός — bad, evil; masc./neut. acc. sg.: ’by an evil (fate)’, inner acc. with μόρον · also neut. nom. sg., subject of an impersonal verb (τι … κακὸν … μελέτω ’let no evil thing be a care’) · also neut. acc. sg. as a plain substantive, direct object: ’harm, evil’ (κακὸν ἀλλοδαποῖσι φέροντες ’bringing harm to men of other lands’) · also neut. acc. sg., attributive with ἦμαρ: ’evil’ (κακὸν ἦμαρ ’the evil day’) · also masc. acc. sg., predicative: ’base, cowardly’ (κακὸν καὶ ἀνήνορα ’base and unmanned’) · also neut. acc. sg. attributive with πῆμα: ’evil’ (πῆμα κακὸν ’evil harm’) · also neut. nom. sg., predicate with an infinitive as subject: κακὸν … βάζειν ’(it is) bad to speak’ · also neut. acc. sg. governed by ἐς: ’into evil’ (ἐς κακὸν … βάλῃσθα) · also neut. acc. sg. subject of an infinitive: ’an evil’ (κακὸν ἔμμεναι ’that an evil is’) · also neut. nom. sg., subject of εἴη: ’evil’ (μή τι κακὸν … εἴη ’and may no evil be’) · also neut. acc. sg., attributive with ῥάκος: ’vile’ (ῥάκος ἄλλο κακὸν ’another, a vile rag’)
__broaden__.κλισίην: κλισίη — seat, chair (general sense); fem. acc. sg. · also hut, shelter (the usual epic sense): ’to my hut’ (ἐς κλισίην ἄγαγον ’I led you to my hut’)
__broaden__.οἷόν: οἷος — such as, of what sort; masc. acc. sg. correlative with τοῖος (τοῖος ἐὼν οἷόν μιν ’just such as when’) · also neut. acc. sg., adverbial and consecutive: ’so that, such that’ (οἷόν σ’ … οὐδέ σε πείθω)
__broaden__.πέμψαι: πέμπω — send, convey; aor. inf. act.: ’to send’ · also inf. used as an imperative: ’send (me)’ (ἕσσας με … πέμψαι)
__broaden__.πυθόμην: πυνθάνομαι — learn, learn by inquiry; aor. mid. 1 sg., unaugmented, in an unreal-past condition: ’I had learned’ · also plain narrative aorist: ’I learned’ (Ὀδυσῆος ἐγὼ πυθόμην ’I learned of Odysseus’)
__broaden__.τάς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. pl.: ’them’, of the Sirens · also ’them’, of the rocks (accented before the enclitic γε) · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: fem. acc. pl. ’which’ (νῆας, τάς οἱ ξυνέαξαν ’ships which … shattered for him’)
__broaden__.τὰς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. pl.: ‘them, those’ (referring to ships) · also fem. acc. pl. ’them’, of the mules · also fem. acc. pl. ’them’, of the cattle · also fem. acc. pl. ’them’, of the fruits · also fem. acc. pl. ’them’, of the nymphs and of the Sirens · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: fem. acc. pl. ’which’ (ἀπειλάων, τὰς … ἐπηπείλησε ’threats which he threatened’) · also fem. acc. pl. ’them’, of the swine

__broaden__.ἡμέτερον: ἡμέτερος — our, ours; neut. acc. sg. · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with κάματον: ’our (toil)’
__broaden__.ὄπισθε: ὄπισθε(ν) — behind, from behind; adv. · also ’hereafter, afterwards’ (of time)

__broaden__.τὰ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’ · also in the adverbial idiom τὰ πρῶτα, ’at first, first’ (not ’these things’) · also with a noun, pointing to it: ’those, the’ (τὰ σὰ γούνατα ’those knees of yours’) · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: which; neut. nom. pl.
